lead.hed: Navy awards Raytheon up to $24.4 billion for more than 1,900 SM-6 missiles
lead.insight: The Navy contracted RTX’s Raytheon to build more than 1,900 Standard Missile-6 interceptors over five years, with two option years, in a deal worth up to $24.4 billion announced Thursday. The SM-6 handles air defense, ballistic-missile defense and ship strikes, and the award follows months of heavy munitions use in the Middle East. The open question is money: Congress still has to appropriate the funds before the plant can invest at full scale.
lead.image_credit: U.S. Navy courtesy photo · DVIDS 8087683 · Public domain · USS Savannah (LCS 28) fires an SM-6 from a containerized launcher in the Eastern Pacific, Oct. 24, 2023.

political.hed: Pentagon tells Senate it will build an area-denial network along the First Island Chain
political.insight: In a Sept. 22 report to the Senate Armed Services Committee on the 2026 National Defense Strategy, the Pentagon restated its plan for a forward-deployed anti-access network along the First Island Chain to deter China. The report also presses the need for more high-end munitions, the same shortfall behind this week’s SM-6 buy.

political.hed: Taiwan receives its first two F-16V Block 70 fighters after years of delay
political.insight: The first two of 66 F-16V Block 70 jets from a 2019 U.S. sale landed at Chihhang Air Base in Taitung on Friday. Software problems held up the $8 billion order. Defense Minister Wellington Koo said more aircraft would arrive soon but gave no schedule.

political.hed: Navy closes fiscal 2026 with at least 45,112 enlisted recruits
political.insight: The Navy’s final numbers show at least 45,112 active-duty enlisted sailors brought in during fiscal 2026, above its 45,000 goal. The service had announced in July that it reached the goal three months early.

political.hed: Heritage argues rising household wealth undercuts the shrinking-middle-class story
political.insight: A Heritage commentary pushes back on the K-shaped-economy account, arguing that gains in home values and retirement savings belong in any measure of how the middle class is doing. It is an economic argument from Heritage, not a new government data release.

tech.hed: France plans to fly fighters with AI-driven combat drones in 2028
tech.insight: France’s Air Force, its armament directorate and the defense AI agency plan a 2028 flight pairing crewed fighters with combat drones under a project called Hypairion. Officials said the aim is government-owned, open software for command and control and mission autonomy, rather than relying on a contractor’s closed system.

culture.hed: Public Discourse marks 75 years of “God and Man at Yale”
culture.insight: Writing on the anniversary of William F. Buckley Jr.’s book, Public Discourse asks whether a university without shared moral reference points can still defend the worth of the human person. The essay is commentary on higher education, not news of a campus decision.

culture.hed: First Things revisits Shakespeare’s King Lear in Stalin’s Russia
culture.insight: A First Things essay looks at how “King Lear” was read and staged under Soviet rule, and what the play’s portrait of power and loyalty meant to people living under it.
